name: American exceptionalism
summary: American exceptionalism holds that the United States is distinctive and exemplary, founded on liberty, equality, individualism, popular government and religious faith, and that it has a special role as a beacon or leader for the world. Adherents see it as a model nation rather than one bound by Old World class divisions.
scope: The mainstream patriotic version from Winthrop and Jefferson through Tocqueville, Lipset and Reagan, in which the US is a free, religious, market-minded republic with a global leadership role. It is not a full program, so many economic and social answers are 0 or low; it excludes the Marxist and postnationalist critical senses of the term.
